name: Lindisfarne Gospels
summary: An illuminated Gospel book created in the Northumbrian monastic tradition.
details: The Lindisfarne Gospels blend Mediterranean, Celtic, Germanic, and Christian visual traditions. The manuscript is a major witness to early medieval religious art and book production.

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: An illuminated Gospel book created in the Northumbrian monastic tradition.
The Lindisfarne Gospels blend Mediterranean, Celtic, Germanic, and Christian visual traditions. The manuscript is a major witness to early medieval religious art and book production.

contentSections.title: Description
paragraphs: Lindisfarne Gospels is a material or textual object whose physical survival helps historians read medieval politics, belief, art, or memory.

contentSections.title: Origin and dating
paragraphs: The archive date of 715 is an orientation point. Exact dating, patronage, or production context may be debated depending on the object.

contentSections.title: Historical context
paragraphs: Lindisfarne Gospels belongs to the world of Lindisfarne, Northumbria, where objects, texts, relics, and images could carry authority across generations.

contentSections.title: Use or meaning
paragraphs: The Lindisfarne Gospels functioned as a sacred book for worship, memory, and monastic prestige at Lindisfarne. Its later Old English gloss also made it a major witness to language, translation, and the continuing life of the manuscript after its original Insular context.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: Lindisfarne Gospels remains a useful witness because it gives material form to medieval culture rather than reducing history to rulers and battles.
